title: Jensen-Shannon divergence — jsdiv
text: Jensen-Shannon divergence, also known capacitory discrimination, symmetric bounded discrimination measure finite-mass positive measures defined measurable space. formally defined, \(p\) \(q\) two finite-mass positive measures, $$\mathbb{JS}(p,q) = \frac{1}{2} \left( \mathbb{K}\left(p: \frac{p+q}{2}  \right) +  \mathbb{K}\left(q: \frac{p+q}{2}  \right)\right),$$ \(\mathbb{K}\) denotes Kullback-Leibler divergence; see kldiv(). probability distributions (pds), linked Shannon entropy \(\mathbb{S}\) relation $$\mathbb{JS}(p,q) = \mathbb{S} \left( \frac{p+q}{2} \right) - \frac{\mathbb{S}(p) + \mathbb{S}(q)}{2}.$$ Properties Jensen-Shannon divergence include: definition pds distinct supports: \(\mathbb{JS}(p,q)\) well-defined wether \(p\) \(q\) support, symmetry: \(\mathbb{JS}(p,q) = \mathbb{JS}(q,p)\), boundedness: \(\mathbb{JS}(p,q) \leq \log(2)\), equality whenever supports \(p\) \(q\) disjoint.
